title: litterfitter
text: key function fit_litter, can fit 6 different types decomposition trajectories: neg.exp, weibull, discrete.parallel, discrete.series, cont.quality neg.exp.limit (see ?fit_litter). fitted object litfit object can visually compare fits different non-linear equations plot_multiple_fits function:  Calling plot litfit object show data, curve fit, even equation, estimated coefficients:  summary litfit object show summary statistics fit. litfit object can see uncertainty parameter estimate bootstrapping  summarise bootstrap distribution parameter (implied steady state) mean quantiles:
code: library(litterfitter) set.seed(1) fit <- fit_litter(   time = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),   mass.remaining = c(1, 0.9, 1.01, 0.4, 0.6, 0.2, 0.01),   model = "weibull",   iters = 500 )  class(fit) plot_multiple_fits(   time = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),   mass.remaining = c(1, 0.9, 1.01, 0.4, 0.6, 0.2, 0.01),   model = c("neg.exp", "weibull"),   iters = 500 ) plot(fit) #> Summary of litFit object #> Model type: weibull  #> Number of observations:  7  #> Parameter fit (beta): 4.19 #> Parameter fit (alpha): 2.47 #> Time to 50% mass loss: 3.61  #> Implied steady state litter mass: 3.71 in units of yearly input  #> AIC:  -3.8883  #> AICc:  -0.8883  #> BIC:  -3.9965 post <- bootstrap_parameters(fit, nboot = 500) plot(post) summary(post) #>                  mean     2.5%      50%     97.5% #> beta         4.145207 3.026793 4.254169  5.150706 #> alpha        4.239639 1.108681 2.664013 10.000000 #> steady_state 3.801316 2.873050 3.791254  4.900035

title: litterfitter
text: fit_litter_all() fits several models data returns together. glance() gives model-comparison table, sorted AICc, difference best model (delta_AICc). use pineneedles data ships package: litfit objects logLik method, base R functions AIC() BIC() also work, e.g. AIC(fits$neg.exp, fits$weibull). tidy(fits) gives parameter estimates every model one table. Note handful observations complex models often poorly identified; see Cornwell & Weedon (2013) discussion.
code: data(pineneedles) fits <- fit_litter_all(   time = pineneedles$Year,   mass.remaining = pineneedles$Mass.remaining,   models = c("neg.exp", "weibull", "discrete.parallel", "cont.quality"),   iters = 500 ) fits #> litfit_list: 4 models fit to 6 observations #>  #>              model nparams logLik    AICc delta_AICc #>            neg.exp       1  9.197 -15.395      0.000 #>            weibull       2  9.459 -10.918      4.477 #>       cont.quality       2  9.197 -10.394      5.001 #>  discrete.parallel       3  9.227  -0.454     14.940 glance(fits)[, c("fit", "nparams", "logLik", "AICc", "delta_AICc", "time_to_50")] #>                 fit nparams   logLik        AICc delta_AICc time_to_50 #> 1           neg.exp       1 9.197395 -15.3947904   0.000000   2.493138 #> 2           weibull       2 9.458945 -10.9178902   4.476900   2.517099 #> 3      cont.quality       2 9.196866 -10.3937318   5.001059   2.490919 #> 4 discrete.parallel       3 9.227192  -0.4543834  14.940407   2.467509

title: litterfitter
text: Every fitted object plot() method using base graphics. Supplying bootstrap adds pointwise uncertainty band, litfit_list plots models together table information criteria:   plot() bootstrap shows distributions; use coef.index = "" see every parameter derived quantity:  ggplot2 installed, autoplot() gives plots ggplot objects, can customised usual layers, scales themes:
code: boot_neg <- bootstrap_parameters(fits$neg.exp, nboot = 500) plot(fits$neg.exp, boot = boot_neg) plot(fits) plot(boot_neg, coef.index = "all") library(ggplot2) autoplot(fits$neg.exp, boot = boot_neg) autoplot(fits) + theme_bw() autoplot(boot_neg)

title: litterfitter
text: tidy(), glance() augment() return fits data frames, following conventions broom package. augment() newdata gives predictions grid times, bootstrap adds pointwise uncertainty band (.lower, .upper): data frames make straightforward build figures, example ggplot2:  compare curves several models, use augment() litfit_list, stacks predictions fit column map colour:
code: best <- fits$neg.exp boot <- bootstrap_parameters(best, nboot = 500) #> Warning in bootstrap_parameters(best, nboot = 500): 5 of 500 bootstrap #> replicates failed and are recorded as NA tidy(best, boot = boot) #>   term estimate  std.error  conf.low conf.high #> 1    k 0.278022 0.01975556 0.2364451 0.3140112 grid <- augment(best, newdata = seq(0, 5, length.out = 100), boot = boot) head(grid) #>         time   .fitted    .lower    .upper #> 1 0.00000000 1.0000000 1.0000000 1.0000000 #> 2 0.05050505 0.9860566 0.9842659 0.9881293 #> 3 0.10101010 0.9723076 0.9687795 0.9763996 #> 4 0.15151515 0.9587504 0.9535366 0.9648091 #> 5 0.20202020 0.9453821 0.9385336 0.9533562 #> 6 0.25252525 0.9322003 0.9237667 0.9420392 library(ggplot2) ggplot(grid, aes(time)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = .lower, ymax = .upper), fill = "grey85") +   geom_line(aes(y = .fitted)) +   geom_point(data = augment(best), aes(y = mass)) +   labs(x = "Time (years)", y = "Proportion mass remaining") curves <- augment(fits, newdata = seq(0, 5, length.out = 100)) ggplot(curves, aes(time, .fitted, colour = fit)) +   geom_line() +   geom_point(data = augment(best), aes(y = mass), colour = "black") +   labs(x = "Time (years)", y = "Proportion mass remaining", colour = "Model")

title: litterfitter
text: fit_element() fits proportion element remaining (example nitrogen, N/N0) changes litter mass lost. Elements often immobilised early decomposition (element remaining rises 1) released later. import.model Parton et al. (2007) describes pattern: plot shows mass remaining decreasing left right, decomposition proceeds along x axis; dashed line marks initial amount element:  glance() reports peak element remaining mass remaining occurs, bootstrapping gives uncertainty:
code: efit <- fit_element(   mass.remaining = pineneedles$Mass.remaining,   element.remaining = c(1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1, 0.8, 0.6),   iters = 500, quiet = TRUE ) efit #> elementfit object: model import.model fit to 6 observations #> Parameters: #>      a      b  #> 0.4920 0.6457  #> Peak element remaining: 1.36 at mass remaining 0.646 #> logLik: 7.608   AIC: -11.217   AICc: -7.217   BIC: -11.633 plot(efit) glance(efit)[, c("model", "AICc", "peak_element", "mass_at_peak")] #>          model      AICc peak_element mass_at_peak #> 1 import.model -7.216568     1.357312    0.6456784 eboot <- bootstrap_parameters(efit, nboot = 500) summary(eboot) #>                   mean      2.5%       50%     97.5% #> a            0.4428565 0.1000000 0.4728605 0.5851202 #> b            0.6415515 0.6156219 0.6383721 0.6770069 #> peak_element 1.7410779 1.3141080 1.3586614 5.0988436 #> mass_at_peak 0.6415417 0.6156127 0.6383652 0.6769985

title: Fits a Collection of Curves to Single-Cohort Decomposition Data
text: key function fit_litter, can fit 6 different types decomposition trajectories. toy example, take litterbag study three replicate bags harvested nine times (years). Decomposition slow first, speeds , often happens decomposers colonise litter: Fit Weibull curve . fitted object litfit object: can visually compare fits different non-linear equations plot_multiple_fits function. single-rate negative exponential capture early lag Weibull curve fits:  Calling plot litfit object show data, curve fit, even equation, estimated coefficients:  summary litfit object show summary statistics fit. Bootstrapping shows uncertainty parameter estimates fitted curve:
code: toy <- data.frame(   time = rep(c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6), each = 3),   mass.remaining = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 0.99, 0.95, 0.96, 0.87, 0.99,                      0.75, 0.83, 0.89, 0.53, 0.6, 0.61, 0.41, 0.35, 0.21,                      0.04, 0.27, 0.17, 0.01, 0.07, 0.15, 0.14, 0.01, 0.02) ) fit <- fit_litter(   time = toy$time,   mass.remaining = toy$mass.remaining,   model = "weibull",   iters = 500 )  class(fit) plot_multiple_fits(   time = toy$time,   mass.remaining = toy$mass.remaining,   model = c("neg.exp", "weibull"),   iters = 500 ) plot(fit) #> Summary of litFit object #> Model type: weibull  #> Number of observations:  27  #> Parameter fit (beta): 2.92 #> Parameter fit (alpha): 2.07 #> Time to 50% mass loss: 2.44  #> Implied steady state litter mass: 2.58 in units of yearly input  #> AIC:  -65.1217  #> AICc:  -64.6217  #> BIC:  -62.53 boot <- bootstrap_parameters(fit, nboot = 500) plot(fit, boot = boot)

title: Fits a Collection of Curves to Single-Cohort Decomposition Data
text: fit_litter_all() fits several models , glance() gives model comparison table. tidy(), glance() augment() return results data frames analysis custom plots: Weibull model strongly preferred . two-pool discrete.series model can produce lag, fits less well despite extra parameter, single-rate neg.exp model fits worst. ggplot2 installed, autoplot() draws fits, model comparisons bootstrap distributions ggplot objects:
code: fits <- fit_litter_all(   time = toy$time,   mass.remaining = toy$mass.remaining,   models = c("neg.exp", "weibull", "discrete.series"),   iters = 500 ) glance(fits)[, c("fit", "nparams", "AICc", "delta_AICc", "time_to_50")] #>               fit nparams      AICc delta_AICc time_to_50 #> 1         weibull       2 -64.62170    0.00000   2.444290 #> 2 discrete.series       3 -50.24970   14.37200   2.341991 #> 3         neg.exp       1 -27.15226   37.46945   2.206548 library(ggplot2) autoplot(fits) + theme_bw()

text: elementfit object, methods print, plot, coef, fitted, residuals, predict, nobs, logLik (AIC() BIC() work), tidy, glance augment, support bootstrap_parameters. elements include optimFit, logLik, fitAIC, fitAICc, fitBIC, mass, element, predicted, model nparams.

title: Fit element (nutrient) dynamics during decomposition — fit_element
text: import.model nitrogen release model Parton et al. (2007), written proportional mass remaining \(x\): $$f(x) = \frac{x/b}{\sqrt{(2ax/b)^2 + (1 - (x/b)^2)^2}}, \qquad   y = f(x) / f(1)$$ curve passes 1 \(x = 1\) (mass lost). \(b\) (bounds 0.01–1) sets mass remaining around immobilisation peak centred, \(\) (bounds 0.1–10) controls height width peak; small \(\) gives tall, narrow peak. original formulation used percent mass remaining (normalised 100, \(b\) 1 100); version equivalent \(b\) divided 100. Fitting uses multi-start likelihood approach fit_litter, gives warnings parameters boundary mass values outside 0–1.

text: returns litfit object following elements: optimFit: list generated optim function logLik: log-likelihood model time: vector time (input) mass: vector mass remaining (input) predicted: predicted values model points within time model: name model nparams: number fit parameters model AIC: AIC model fit AICc: AICc model fit BIC: BIC model fit potentially useful things

title: Fit different models to single cohort decomposition data — fit_litter
text: model likelihood maximized using methods available optim.  Optimization methods used within optim can specified control object (.e., control$method).  default method L-BFGS-B bounds specific model. model neg.exp classic negative exponential model–one parameter (Olson 1963) weibull Weibull residence time model–two parameters (Frechet 1927) discrete.parallel Two pools parallel term fraction initial mass pool–three parameter (Manzoni et al. 2012) discrete.series three parameter model possibility two sequential pools (Manzoni et al. 2012) cont.quality (Ågren Bosatta 1996, see also Manzoni et al. 2012) neg.exp.limit negative exponential decaying towards non-zero asymptote (\(e^{-kt} + B\))–three parameters Warning: difficulty finding optimal solution determined interaction nature complexity likelihood space (data- model-dependent) well optimization methods.  can never guarantee optimal solution found, using many random starting points increase odds.  noted significant variation among models identifiability, models inherently less identifiable likely due tendency form flat ridges likelihood space.  confidence fit low cases (see Cornwell Weedon 2013).   number random starting points used optimization given iters.  function checks whether best 5 optimizations converged likelihood, function return warning. Values outside 0–1: measurement error, especially early decomposition decomposition slow, can produce proportional mass remaining values slightly 1 (.e. negative mass loss). values kept fit, since removing truncating bias estimates, fit_litter warns (class litterfitter_mass_above_one). data also show little overall mass loss, warning notes parameters may poorly constrained derived quantities time_to_prop_mass_remaining steady_state extrapolations. Slightly negative values (-0.1) similarly kept warning (class litterfitter_mass_below_zero). Use suppressWarnings(..., classes = ...) silence checked.

title: litterfitter 0.2.0 (GitHub only; not released to CRAN)
text: fit_litter() now defaults model = "neg.exp" model given. fit_litter() warns mass remaining values 1 0 (see Bug fixes). Fits can differ slightly earlier versions smaller optimiser step. steady_state() returns Inf neg.exp.limit fits B > 0 (previously string). time_to_prop_mass_remaining() returns NA (warning) threshold never reached, result now exact rather read grid, values may differ slightly. coef() now returns named vector.

title: litterfitter 0.2.0 (GitHub only; not released to CRAN)
text: fit_litter() now defaults model = "neg.exp" rejects unknown model names (previously omitting model gave “first argument length > 1”). Proportional mass remaining values 1 (apparent mass gain measurement error, common early decomposition decomposition slow) kept fit now trigger informative warning class litterfitter_mass_above_one; data also show little overall mass loss warning says parameters may poorly constrained derived quantities extrapolations (#21). Slightly negative values (-0.1) kept litterfitter_mass_below_zero warning; clearly negative values percentages errors. fit_litter() now rejects infinite values, invalid iters, data single time point; drops missing observations warning; requires observations parameters. Boundary warnings now name parameters bound, hint default bounds assume time years time values large. Litter fits bootstrap replicates use analytic gradients six curves (#27), improving accuracy small rates rates per day. discrete.series now supports equal pool rates. Element fits calls gr = NULL use finite differences (default ndeps = 1e-4). Built-gradients use default limit 500 optimizer iterations cont.quality fits can converge along shallow minimum. explicit control$maxit takes precedence. local benchmark pineneedles (median three fixed-seed runs), 200-start discrete.series fit took 0.078 s versus 0.109 s previously, 200 bootstrap replicates took 0.053 s versus 0.080 s. Weibull fits bootstraps require strictly positive lower bound scale parameter beta. Bootstrap replicates reach optimizer’s iteration limit otherwise fail converge recorded NA. “may found global best fit” check now compares 5 best fits (previously compared 5 worst) longer errors fewer 5 starts succeed. steady_state() neg.exp.limit now returns number (Inf B > 1e-4, otherwise / k) instead string, fixing errors summary() bootstrap_parameters(). bootstrap_parameters() records failed replicates NA instead erroring. time_to_prop_mass_remaining() now uses uniroot(): exact, fast, independent time units, returns NA warning threshold never reached. Plot curves use fixed number points regardless time units; plot_multiple_fits() longer clips mass values 1. Fixed Weibull discrete.series formula display plot.litfit(). plot.litfit() always shows (0, 1) starting point y axis (#7). six models now documented ?fit_litter; neg.exp accidentally commented neg.exp.limit missing (#22). time_to_prop_mass_remaining() gives clear error missing threshold.mass. Restored input-validation tests lost 0.1.5, greatly expanded test suite (edge cases inputs, every model, derived quantities checked closed-form results, bootstrap failures, methods plots).
